findings.title: Preserve complete historical read-range objects when merging new observations
findings.trigger: A valid prior canonical row contains a read_ranges member such as {"start_line":1,"end_line":1,"content_digest":"sha256:historical-content"}, and read-observations.json adds an exact-source observation for that row. The content_digest member is explicitly allowed by source-inventory.schema.json:203-205.
findings.cause: apply_literal_read_observations reduces every prior and new range to a two-element start/end tuple, then constructs fresh objects containing only those two fields. Thus an existing content_digest is discarded even when the old span and source identity are unchanged.
findings.effect: The materializer silently deletes permitted historical per-range evidence. The normal source schema and subsequent strict gates still accept the derived row because content_digest is optional; the generated candidate and persisted shards therefore no longer retain the original range record. This contradicts the task and helper contract to preserve existing reading history. The present 34 observed rows have empty prior ranges, so this finding does not claim that this exact batch has already destroyed a stored digest.
findings.fix: Preserve the original range objects, including their metadata, and append only genuinely new observation ranges with deterministic, idempotent handling. Deduplication must not collapse or erase different historical records that share endpoints. Keep the existing identity, depth, pending-mapping and strict post-materialization gates unchanged.
findings.required_oracle: Extend the existing Actions-only materialization contract with a digest-bearing prior range plus an overlapping or identical new observation; assert the complete historical range object survives both the first and second expand/shard pass. The current preservation test uses only start/end ranges and therefore cannot detect this loss.
findings.proof_type: Static source and schema counterexample; no local executable validation performed
